https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
While the Trump administration and RFK Jr. undermine vaccine safety from Washington, states like Colorado are stepping up to protect public health.
And Georgia could be doing the same — with the right leadership.
As a scientist and someone who has spent my time in office fighting for evidence-based policy, it breaks my heart to watch politicians play games with public health. Casting doubt on vaccine safety doesn’t just create confusion — it leads to real harm, especially for children, seniors, and immunocompromised families.
Colorado is showing what responsible leadership looks like: putting science first, protecting access, and ensuring communities stay safe.
Georgia deserves nothing less.
That’s why I’m asking you to add your name to my petition calling on Georgia lawmakers to defend vaccine access, reject political interference, and stand firmly with science.
We can build a state where our leaders protect families instead of pandering to conspiracy theorists — but only if we make our voices impossible to ignore.
Will you add your name today and join me in demanding that Georgia stand up for science? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Pu8ayb7DR0OXEfSM9edl5w2]

Speaker Mike Johnson came to Southwest Washington to campaign for my opponent, John Braun.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
That tells you everything you need to know.
Mike Johnson didn't come here because he's worried about our roads. He didn't come here because he wants to help small businesses stay open. He didn't come here because he cares about lowering costs for working families.
He came here because Washington Republicans think they can buy, bully, and nationalize this district.
And hey, you don’t just have to take it from me:
Mike Johnson said it himself: "Washington's Third District is going to help decide the fate of the republic." He called this race "a big one" and pointed to the Cook Political Report's list of just 18 toss-up House races , with ours right at the top. Then he made their goal crystal clear: if John Braun wins, Republicans will keep—and grow—their House majority.
This race isn't just on their radar—it's one of their highest priorities.
They want another reliable vote. Another member of Congress who will do what party leaders tell him. Another politician who answers to Washington instead of Southwest Washington.
That's not why you sent me to Congress.
You sent me there to fight for Southwest Washington—even when it's unpopular. To stand up for our timber communities. To protect the right to repair. To support local manufacturers and small businesses. To put this district ahead of any political party.
Now they're sending the Speaker of the House into our backyard because they think this seat belongs to them.
It doesn't.
It belongs to the people who live here.
Today, we have an opportunity to send Mike Johnson, John Braun, and every DC insider a message they won't forget:
Southwest Washington isn't for sale.
We won't be bullied.
And we won't let outside politicians decide who represents our communities.
Will you rush a contribution of $5 or whatever you can right now to help us send that message loud and clear? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Every dollar we raise today is proof that this campaign belongs to the people of Southwest Washington—not the political machine in Washington, D.C.
Let's show them what this district is made of.
Thank you,
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez

Hi, I have to get up early a lot nowadays, and there’s not much that beats the first cup of coffee of the day.

But when you’re running in a high-stakes Senate race like this one – where anything can happen at any given moment – the nights are just as important as the mornings.

Right now, Patrick (my campaign manager) is texting me live updates about where things stand with our fundraising, and I’ve got a list of things we have to do first thing tomorrow. **In the meantime, though, I told him I’d reach out to my top supporters and see if they could lend a hand.**

[**_If you’re able to spare a few bucks before you hit the hay, please chip in here._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136996713/639333698/-1037742479?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_t1nd_jtk5744&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MGZlNDI5Mi0yNTk1LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hdbM99HlYlUWu9ZBD4-Ht4ZUzz8UmtpWN-8ss0Sy7bg=)

Reflection comes easy at night, and I’m thinking back to all the conversations I’ve had on the campaign trail so far.

Ohioans, like folks all across the country, are worried about rising costs. They’re fed up with the corruption and power grabs happening in Washington. They’re frustrated with DC politicians like Jon Husted who have left them in the dust.

Yet through it all, so many folks are showing up at our campaign events, or they’re knocking on doors with their neighbors, or they’re stopping for a quick chat with me, because **they believe that we _can_ do better.**

With experts at _The Cook Political Report_ ,_MS NOW_ , and even _Fox News_ calling this race a “Toss Up,” we have an incredible opportunity to flip this battleground seat – and the Senate – but it won’t be easy.

# Your Private Invitation: Waterfront Home Dinner.
Dear Maryland friend, You know it. We know it. Everyone seems to understand it. Maryland is at a cross-roads for our destiny and the future of our families, property, businesses and everything that we've worked hard to build.

The next three months will determine the direction of the next four years.

Wes Moore has in the last few weeks given us a Triple Kick to the Gut.

He lost the Triple Crown, with its exclusion from the Thoroughbred Championship because of failed negotiations. Instead, he sunk over $600 million into buying the Maryland horse-racing industry with your tax money. What a waste.

The Key Bridge is now not likely to be built before 2031. [Come hear ](https://us.list-manage.com/J3ZQkaO97ye?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)my first-hand knowledge of why that is true.

And now he wants to take our last voice of opposition - the First District Congressional seat.

[Join me tomorrow night](https://us.list-manage.com/fq1QEVOrkba?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) with Governor Ehrlich, Ed & Cindy Hartman and Jeff & Melanie Dunaway at a private waterfront home dinner.

Come hear me discuss my recent trip to the Republican Governor's Association retreat, my meetings with the nation's top Governors, and my discussions with attendees at that event who have recently met with Wes Moore, providing inside information into important issues and pending matters not otherwise known to the public.

Come also to hear the breaking information showing why we will win this November with your help.

Please [join us](https://us.list-manage.com/NBU_4kHX5SA?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) tomorrow night. See you there!
For Maryland,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Maryland Governor

| Team,

**Leaders We Deserve is going to be the super PAC to end all super PACs.**

_Citizens United_ has flooded our democracy with corporate cash, dark money, and special interest influence for over a decade. And the only way to fix it permanently is to elect leaders who will fight to overturn it with the urgency it demands.

But until that happens, we can’t send our candidates into races against opponents flush with unlimited corporate money, and tell them to fight with both hands behind their backs. That’s _not_ a winning strategy.

**We play the game we have, and use the tools of a broken system to beat it in its own arena.** And we keep fighting until the system that makes this necessary no longer exists.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a1b0f3fb-f870-43e6-8d91-793cbeb0cdc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

In the river of incoherent "takes" and information we are all made to swim in, this is my life raft: Every so often, I revise a list of facts that seem to point to more durable features of our political terrain. I include facts about public opinion if they appear to reflect a consistent and settled understanding.
I spent some time this week updating my list, so here's a first take on the 2026 Midterm Edition of Essential Facts. These are not meant to be predictive of anything and are listed in no particular order:
This post is free because these facts are important. You can still support more work like this by becoming a paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..5p4owNG1dkQuppObNweC6ykjtNv5HYn9jb2NCKwFXJE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=210609972)
* Before the Iran War started, [less than half](https://substack.com/redirect/859dc57d-48f5-4b9e-b6ee-89be6812e79e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Americans had enough cash to cover an emergency $1,000 expense.
* Research [completed just last week](https://substack.com/redirect/a9feaf6a-f9ef-45d4-9e9e-4d4ec5fd935d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows Democrats have opened up an 8-point advantage on handling the cost of living. We were even with Republicans at the start of the year. Good, but it's only 35-27 now.
* This year, the share of our national income earned by workers hit a new low, while the share booked as corporate profits hit a new high. (I was surprised coverage of this in the [Wall Street Journal (gift link)](https://substack.com/redirect/9d82492c-fbec-4bfd-a7aa-f08f40306f60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was not a bigger story.)
* The most [popular](https://substack.com/redirect/35ac8531-810c-4536-a1ab-95ebde0c36bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) elected official among Democrats in America, by far, is Bernie Sanders (and he is not even a Democrat!). The second is AOC. Important when you try to make sense of primaries.
* Half of Pennsylvania Democrats have a positive view of the Democratic Socialists of America. Only 15% have an unfavorable view. (Your support helped me access some private research I can't link here. Thank you!)
* Even though the DSA draws its votes mostly from [highly educated](https://substack.com/redirect/b97891a7-6af0-4228-bd41-8be82b46d693?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) voters, I am choosing to believe most of these Pennsylvanians don't know that one of the chairs of the DSA just [told](https://substack.com/redirect/3d92fb09-c74e-47e8-a709-2fc45b9f8e98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The New Yorker that the mass slaughter, rape, and kidnapping of Jews in Israel on October 7 was "largely inevitable," and reaffirmed her support for those who rallied for Hamas in New York the day after the attack.
* I asked Claude to make this table comparing Trump's current popularity to Biden's in 2022, and you can see how similar they are, with Trump actually holding his party slightly better. Notable since '22 was decent for Biden:

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e44f31f5-93e6-4968-ab94-e01bbd10ef6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* On the other hand, enthusiasm to vote among Republicans has [dropped dramatically](https://substack.com/redirect/5335f27f-4a95-4ea1-adae-7e84089c2f19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and seems to be worse than Democrats' enthusiasm in 2022, and worse than Republicans' own enthusiasm in 2018.
* Can money buy back any of that enthusiasm? Outside of each side's candidate campaign accounts, Republicans have at least _**three times**_ as much money as the Democrats, which is different than previous cycles. This chart from [Politico](https://substack.com/redirect/00665ed1-dfb1-4da6-beeb-30bc7fd60fd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sums up it pretty well:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a6d44739-1a3a-4afb-8516-8dfae062b019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* Some say a "wave" could overcome these dynamics, which is true, but people tend to forget that ticket-splitting still happens to a significant degree:
* In 2020, Susan Collins (who won) got almost 57,000 more votes than Donald Trump (who lost), which was about 7%. Decisive.
* Mid-term electorates are different, but note that in 2022 Democrat Josh Shapiro and Republican Brian Fitzpatrick each carried the same congressional district by [double](https://substack.com/redirect/c424c8dd-d8bd-485e-998c-8e603bf48130?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) digits.
* 2022 also reminds us how the mid-term pattern of the President's party losing power is a [less dependable](https://substack.com/redirect/ef4d38f6-a861-48db-b5cf-13ce795f008f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) pattern for Senate races than for House races.
* To take control of the Senate in 2026, Democrats need to hang on to _both_ Michigan and Georgia, _and_ win at least four of these six: Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Iowa, Alaska, Texas. (Then, we'd need to hope Fetterman didn't flip to become a Republican and give back control of the chamber.). A tall order.
* While these states are hard to win, you should not think of them as one-off exceptions. They are the new map. The 2030 redistricting will [shift more representation](https://substack.com/redirect/74911a70-58ec-43e4-87b1-1f085c451727?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Sun Belt and make it impossible for Democrats to win the White House purely with its old "blue wall" strategy.
* Education is emerging as [the critical divide](https://substack.com/redirect/b3fb5d07-52c2-4791-ae77-a940d1992680?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in American politics, with 2024 having the highest level of educational polarization seen yet.
* Of the six states I mentioned above, five are below the national average in percentage of voters with a bachelor's degree.
* Yet Nevada is even further below the national average than these five, and Democrats control both of its Senate seats.
* Two years ago, Democrats held a Senate seat in the state with the lowest percentage of bachelor's degree holders in the entire country. His name was Joe Manchin.
* A Democrat who succeeded with working-class voters more recently was definitely not a DSA member: In 2025, Gov. Abigail Spanberger won [half](https://substack.com/redirect/8dee117c-c7a2-45f8-813f-74fa4b9308e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of these voters, a significant number considering Harris won 42% in 2024.
* Also in 2025, [Cuomo beat Mamdani](https://substack.com/redirect/bb8999a3-c53a-4784-bb8e-38a6c66bff2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among voters without a college degree.
* Last month, Susan Collins was beating Platner [among working-class voters](https://substack.com/redirect/124f7d9d-3f92-4f60-a3e4-af128e183dbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by more than 20 (he was getting 37%), and Stevens was beating El-Sayed by a similar amount.

Hope this is helpful. How about a [quote](https://substack.com/redirect/903aef87-c555-4a32-9a19-d7037059e55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the late, great Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan to close?
> There is a center in American politics. It can govern. The [National Commission on Social Security Reform] is just an example of what can be done. First, get your facts straight. Everyone is entitled to his own opinion, but not his own facts. Second, decide to live with the facts. Third, resolve to surmount them. Because, fourth, what is at stake is our capacity to govern.

| | |

Peter, This is Kaitlin, Rick’s campaign manager. I’m reaching out because we need your help to hit our goal by this week’s deadline. By Thursday at midnight, we need to raise another $17,350 so the campaign can keep reaching Mainers with Rick’s message at a moment when more people are paying attention and looking for real leadership. **Can you make a contribution right now to help us hit this goal by Thursday at midnight?**

---
Right now, Mainers are paying more and more for energy while powerful interests profit. Rick has a plan to change that. He'll lower delivery costs by reining in excessive utility profits, he’ll expand energy efficiency efforts, and he’ll make sure the benefits of Maine's renewable resources stay here at home. Rick’s plan will lower energy bills – and he has the experience to get it done. This is the kind of plan that connects, because it speaks directly to what we are all dealing with every month – the cost to heat our homes, keep the lights on, and stay afloat. **But strong ideas only matter if we have the resources to get them in front of voters.** We need to raise another $17,350 by Thursday at midnight to run more of our digital ads, expand voter outreach, and put Rick’s vision for a more affordable future in front of more Mainers right now. Can you chip in before Thursday at midnight to help us get there?
---

name: The Angry Democrats: Matt Diemer & Laura Rodriguez-Carbone
subject: Dems Choice of S.C. for First Primary Slot Signal of who they will push for 2028 Presidential Ticket
body:
| |
---|---|---
| | | | | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/redirect/52557aba-7733-45b6-887b-2c95851fc9d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) cross-posted a post from [The Whisper Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/d8df3c6c-0823-47d1-9a33-da4f8139c129?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---|---|---
| | | The Angry DemocratAug 11 * The Angry Democrat
---|---|---
Check this out from the Whisper Campaign.

Laura wrote a really interesting analysis laying out five filters the Democratic Party is using to determine who could be the next presidential nominee. One way the party could enact one of those filters is by making South Carolina the first primary state.

Laura brilliantly explains why that matters and what it could mean for the field.

Some of the 2028 Presidential hopefuls for the Democratic Party
The Democratic National Committee's Rules and Bylaws Committee voted to keep South Carolina at the front of the 2028 presidential primary calendar. The early primary window expanded from five states to six. The primary order now runs [South Carolina on January 22, Nevada on February 1, New Hampshire on February 8, New Mexico on February 15, Michigan on February 22, and Virginia on February 29](https://substack.com/redirect/86247ce0-1d31-4218-bd82-1749d3515c64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with Super Tuesday on March 7, 2028. [New Mexico and Virginia are in the early window for the first time](https://substack.com/redirect/e9722e34-1f83-4499-9071-f5c7a9d9b723?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On the new order, [members of the panel invoked Black Americans' long struggle for voting rights and the need to build political power in the South](https://substack.com/redirect/86247ce0-1d31-4218-bd82-1749d3515c64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [several said South Carolina's position gained salience after the Supreme Court further gutted the Voting Rights Act earlier this year](https://substack.com/redirect/cc96279e-d941-481e-8816-540225ac0d71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That argument is real and valid, but there is another read on this most people are missing and no one is writing about.
The order of the primary is a tell on where the party is focused on picking up votes. Based on the lay of the land for the 2026 midterms cycle, as well as the shift we've seen to a male-dominated brand strategy for the party nationwide, we can apply five basic filters to narrow down the field of likely Presidential candidates. And there will be many and at last count, I am confident there will be at least 20 Democratic challengers.
These Democrats are: Kamala Harris, Gavin Newsom, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Pete Buttigieg, Cory Booker, Ruben Gallego, Chris Murphy, Wes Moore, Andy Beshear, Jon Ossoff, Raphael Warnock, JB Pritzker, Ro Khanna, Mark Kelly, Tim Walz, Amy Klobuchar, Gretchen Whitmer, Josh Shapiro, Roy Cooper, Rahm Emanuel.
Applying all five filters to these 20 candidates reduces the field from 20 to 2.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/65db4336-e696-4428-a7ec-ebf5779c42f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### Filter 1: The Black Church as a Foundation
[Black voters make up about 60 percent of South Carolina's Democratic primary electorate](https://substack.com/redirect/cccb4566-c1fe-42bc-a05a-9b49d42d4d86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That number is why the state is first, and it is where most analysis of this decision stops. I am going further.
[Pew finds 84 percent of Black Protestants identify with or lean Democratic](https://substack.com/redirect/9eda1bd3-78ce-4224-9c11-7b75262bc58e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and it finds something that matters more for a primary. [Among white adults, Republicans attend services more often than Democrats. Among Black Americans no such gap exists, and Black adults across every religious background are strongly Democratic. Black adults who attend services at least yearly are significantly more likely than attenders in the general population to say they have heard sermons about voting, protesting, and civic engagement](https://substack.com/redirect/30896a51-9726-496e-9a77-0c9af15ae64c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The Black church in South Carolina is an organized, politically active distribution network, where candidates get introduced and where an endorsement travels with weight. When Joe Biden needed the state in 2024, [he campaigned at a barbershop and spoke at a luncheon at a Black church](https://substack.com/redirect/cccb4566-c1fe-42bc-a05a-9b49d42d4d86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He leaned heavily on Senator Jim Clyburn that most people acknowledge has the strongest influence on this network.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8b3a1732-7628-418a-8d4d-8520b7514a27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Representative Ro Khanna and Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear attend South Carolina Senator Jim Clyburn's Fish Fry in May.
Senator Jim Clyburn endorsed Biden days before the 2020 primary, and [that endorsement rescued a collapsing campaign and carried him to the presidency](https://substack.com/redirect/4615e4d0-9675-4ae4-83c1-464b15f16746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He has been picking sides far longer. [He backed Hillary Clinton over Bernie Sanders in 2016, stayed formally neutral in 2008 while being seen as tacitly supporting Barack Obama, and chose John Kerry over fellow Southerner John Edwards in 2004](https://substack.com/redirect/f01a244c-4252-4136-9e8c-e55de7ac1476?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Asked whether his fish fry was really world famous, Clyburn told NPR: "Well, it's my world."
Two months ago, [the 34th annual World Famous Fish Fry featured Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear and Representative Ro Khanna](https://substack.com/redirect/10d47c2e-9627-494d-9d09-ace26db81378?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Gavin Newsom [spent the day before his memoir's release doing meet-and-greets in Berkeley and Clarendon counties before a Rock Hill event moderated by former DNC chair Jaime Harrison](https://substack.com/redirect/4816e907-5fb1-4ba0-9cc2-46473d9b49bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Wes Moore keynoted the Blue Palmetto Dinner and [opened by calling Clyburn the voice that has driven more change than any other](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b3df80-1a88-4ca8-99e2-9ca90d4dd246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This church network should also tell you something else. A candidate who spends a year working South Carolina pulpits comes out the other side fluent in a language the party has not spoken in a generation. Faith vocabulary is a rare political asset that travels. The same cadence that lands in a sanctuary in Orangeburg lands in a Sunday school room in Paducah, and it reaches a bloc the party has written off entirely. [Pew puts white evangelical voters at 85 percent Republican against 14 percent Democratic](https://substack.com/redirect/9eda1bd3-78ce-4224-9c11-7b75262bc58e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That's the theory the party is testing right now. [A striking number of clergy are running for office as Democrats, including three ministers running for Congress in Iowa alone](https://substack.com/redirect/216c29c7-4c83-4289-90c6-71cf7212c4f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Andy Beshear and his wife are both deacons at their Disciples of Christ church in Louisville. His forthcoming book is titled _Go and Do Likewise_ , after the Parable of the Good Samaritan. He blames his own party for the gap with churches, arguing Democrats stopped explaining their motivations in the terms religious voters use, and he told the AP that [his faith is his authentic why](https://substack.com/redirect/216c29c7-4c83-4289-90c6-71cf7212c4f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

#### Filter Two: A Moderate Democrat
The party has told you what it thinks wins. [The DCCC's 2026 recruitment strategy sought candidates resembling a small group of moderate Democrats who have shown they can win where Trump performed well](https://substack.com/redirect/90425039-f9af-42d0-8164-82af66e30a6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including seats Trump carried by 17 points.
An institution that spends two years telling itself moderates are the answer does not switch theories for the presidential cycle. It scales them up. That removes the Democratic Party putting up anyone in the progressive wing on ideological grounds alone, regardless of what those candidates are polling.
You can watch this theory operate on individual candidates in real time. James Talarico spent years in the Texas legislature calling to tear ICE down and describing the border as a welcome mat. [The month he launched his Senate campaign, he recast himself as a border security Democrat, telling a podcast host he had called out Biden for failing to secure the border, and softening his positions on guns and transgender issues in the same interview](https://substack.com/redirect/6761caf1-db3a-4d4d-910b-12127b7da2f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [He now runs a Frontera Tour of the Rio Grande promising a mix of barriers and surveillance technology](https://substack.com/redirect/d3934024-5699-4382-a285-8025e1c3f19d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The same conversion, on the same issues, is running through red-state Democratic campaigns across the map this cycle. The recruitment push Democrats have branded a masculinity strategy has a policy half that gets less attention, and this is it: candidates entering Trump-won races and shedding the progressive positions that made them targets. That is the substance under what the party means when it says a candidate can win in Trump country.

#### Filter Three: From a State Trump Won
A moderate record is a claim anyone can make in a primary. Winning a state Trump carried is evidence nobody can argue with, and the party has decided that's the evidence it needs.
Beshear won the Kentucky governorship twice, in a state Trump carried in 2024 by roughly 30 points. Ossoff holds a Senate seat in Georgia, which Trump carried, and defends it this November. Neither man has to argue he can win Trump voters.
A blue-state Democrat cannot make that case no matter how disciplined a moderate he runs. So this filter clears the field substantially: Gavin Newsom governs California, which Harris won by roughly 20 points, and no matter how far he goes to sound moderate, a Californian asking Kentucky to trust his read in Trump country is making an argument, not pointing at a result. Pete Buttigieg now runs out of Michigan, a state Harris lost, but he has never carried it or anything like it on a ballot, and a competitive mayoralty in Indiana a decade ago is not the credential the party is looking for.
JB Pritzker governs Illinois and Tim Walz governs Minnesota, both comfortably blue, both men who would have to explain why their record is sellable to moderate voters. Amy Klobuchar has won Minnesota by margins of twenty and thirty points, while Harris carried it by four, proving she is popular at home in a blue state, not that she can drag Republican voters across the party line. Cory Booker represents New Jersey, which the party now watches with genuine worry after Harris carried it by six, but watching a state slip is not the same as a Democrat proving he can win where it already went red. Rahm Emanuel is Illinois. Chris Murphy is Connecticut. Both safe, both disqualified by the same logic.
Gavin Newsom, Rahm Emmanuel, Amy Klobuchar, Tim Walz, Cory Booker, Wes Moore, Pete Buttigieg, and Chris Murphy - all from blue states, and all eliminated based on this filter

### Filter four: What the Democratic Party Means by Electability
I want to be exact about whose reasoning I am describing. This is not my read of what American voters will accept, rather its the operating theory of the people who recruit and clear candidates for national races. That theory holds that the voters Democrats lost are men who went to Trump, and that winning them back requires a candidate who looks like them.

### Filter Five Will Test the Progressive/Moderate Divide on Israel
By now you may have noticed we have winnowed our list from 20 names to just three: Senator Jon Ossoff, Senator Mark Kelly, and Governor Andy Bashear. A combination of these three names is what the Democratic institution will want on the ticket for 2028. But they will have to content with a 5th filter, being pushed up by the base: Israel.
[Pew found in April that 80 percent of Democrats hold an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 69 percent a year earlier and 53 percent in 2022](https://substack.com/redirect/40ee5e8f-4e2e-43a2-bb55-22530736b23a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [A New York Times-Siena poll in May found 24 percent of Democrats support additional aid to Israel while 68 percent oppose it](https://substack.com/redirect/ebb59f54-aef5-4213-8f17-06b06738b8f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Gallup has American favorability toward Israel falling from 75 percent in 2021 to 46 percent in 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/e49115aa-4963-4e6c-bf61-2b9b1dbcdea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Additionally, and perhaps more importantly, [Three-fifths of American Jews view Netanyahu unfavorably, and white evangelicals are the only major religious group where a majority still views the Israeli government favorably](https://substack.com/redirect/e49115aa-4963-4e6c-bf61-2b9b1dbcdea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[A House floor vote in July month split Democrats and their own leadership over cutting military aid to Israel, with Nancy Pelosi saying afterward that US policy must change and the Netanyahu government cannot maintain its current course. In New Jersey, an organizer who ran openly against AIPAC won a February special election after AIPAC affiliates spent millions attacking her](https://substack.com/redirect/40ee5e8f-4e2e-43a2-bb55-22530736b23a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Abdul al-Sayed won the Michigan Senatorial primary on Tuesday, a huge upset for AIPAC-backed Haley Stevens.
### How the Calendar Fits the Narrative
South Carolina is the coronation. Whoever the brokers move behind on January 22 gets the coalescence that follows, the endorsements, the money, the donors who were waiting for a signal, and the press narrative that the race is effectively over. The field will thin fast, the way it did for Biden in 2020, and the moderate winner will spend February being sold as inevitable by the Democratic machine.
Michigan is seen, rightly, as a cross section of the American midwest, and where the moderate views on Israel will be tested. It comes third, close enough to the front to matter and late enough that the nominee is already presumed. It asks one question of whoever is left in the primary: who among them can hold the November electorate and bridge the divide between progressive and moderates on Gaza. A nominee who cannot bridge this divide is a nominee who cannot carry Michigan, and likely will not be able to carry the country in the general election. But the party is betting that inevitability and vibes will turn out Democrats in droves larger than who stayed home or voted for Trump in Michigan in 2024.

### The 2028 Presidential Ticket Prediction
[Pew found 61 percent of veteran registered voters backed Trump over Harris in 2024 against 37 percent for Harris, and 63 percent of veteran voters lean Republican](https://substack.com/redirect/ce9fb7f7-ee31-4b1e-82d9-370a545e31f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On November 18, 2025, six Democratic lawmakers made a video reminding service members they can refuse illegal orders. [Trump called it seditious behavior punishable by death](https://substack.com/redirect/6f8a2f95-42cf-4297-a246-1e84054940fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Six days later [the Pentagon opened a review of Kelly and raised recall to active duty for court-martial as a possible outcome](https://substack.com/redirect/e10fc6d0-0b8b-4019-b036-b4c9329eba8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Hegseth noting Kelly was the only one of the six still subject to military law. Then it collapsed. [Hegseth announced no recall and no military proceedings, only a retirement-grade determination to demote a sitting senator and cut his pension](https://substack.com/redirect/1bf766bc-3d53-4650-8a89-1c324e3ee326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Kelly sued. [On February 12, 2026, Judge Richard Leon, a George W. Bush appointee, blocked the Pentagon, writing that it had trampled Kelly's First Amendment freedoms and threatened the liberties of millions of military retirees](https://substack.com/redirect/cafc0919-f930-4476-9494-65b054a116b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Mark Kelly is who will balance the 2028 ticket. An elder, moderate statesman with built in credibility, astronaut, veteran, husband of Gabby Giffords is pathway the party will use to bring back veteran voters. He will be the VP candidate no matter who else is in the race. The party can also afford him, since [his term ends January 3, 2029](https://substack.com/redirect/c7a03df4-ca8e-4596-bcda-4059d9a461af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and he is on the ballot in 2028 regardless. No appointed replacement, no special election, no seat handed to a governor.
Based on the timeline, trends, and strategists own admissions, your 2028 presidential ticket will either be:
**Beshear-Kelly or Ossoff-Kelly.**
Nothing is set in stone, but Democrats are not known for changing their tactics. This is where they are looking right now.
